# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 17: A Free AI Model on Your Desk Takes 37 Years to Break Even


### Our first Free Weights Friday prices open models per $10, Nvidia signs for $390B of supplies and $118B of customers’ bills, B300s go up for resale, and a bitcoin miner leases its campus to an AI lab.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 20, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/5pyszAt4zMzobUeldyzz27) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/1FRiGUMTzHk) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week: our first


**Free Weights Friday** asks whether to own the box or rent the tokens for an open model. Owning loses on price, by a retirement party.


**Nvidia** has committed


**$390 billion** to its suppliers and guarantees up to


**$118 billion** of its customers’ data center bills; Nvidia meal-preps. A compute exchange says


**B300** capacity booked for Chinese-affiliated buyers is up for resale in the US and Western Europe. One careful owner.


**Riot Platforms** , a bitcoin miner, signed the biggest lease in its history, with an AI lab; the best mining is landlording. And the Department of Token Efficiency has three cuts: sorted JSON keys, caching, and a Mac Mini with a job. Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## Free Weights Friday


The weights are free. The gym is where they get you.


Free weights are open models: anyone can download the file. The question is where to run it, and who charges what. One unit today:


**how many output tokens $10 buys** . More is better.


**The desk.** Apple’s


**Mac Studio** with an M5 Max and 128 GB of memory is


**$5,399** at


[Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-mac/mac-studio) . For a free model. One user benchmarked that chip on OpenAI’s open model,


**gpt-oss-120b** , at


**92 tokens a second** (


[oMLX benchmark](https://omlx.ai/benchmarks/performance/m65w0vhz) ). Faster than your coworker answers a quick question.


Run it eight hours a day for three years, power included, and


**$10 of that Mac buys about 5 million output tokens** . Our estimate (the Mac’s price spread over those hours, plus 150 W at $0.18 a kWh, no resale).


**The rent.** The same model, on OpenRouter’s list of hosts (


[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-oss-120b/providers) ), on Thursday:


-


**Together AI** , at $0.60 per million output tokens:


**about 16.7 million** per $10.


-


**The cheapest hosts we found, like Near AI** , at $0.15 per million:


**about 67 million** per $10. That’s a squeezed four-bit version. The model packed a carry-on.


**So on price, owning loses.** Spend the Mac’s $5,399 at Near AI instead and you get about


**36 billion tokens** . The Mac makes about 2.65 million a day at eight hours, so it needs about


**37 years** to make that many. Our estimate. Break-even arrives right around your retirement party.


You own the box for control. No rate limits, except your power company. And the model never changes under you: nobody can sunset a file on your hard drive.


**The other desk box.** Nvidia’s


**DGX Spark** has the same 128 GB. It launched in October 2025 at


**$3,999** (


[Nvidia](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-dgx-spark-arrives-for-worlds-ai-developers) ). Nvidia’s own store now lists it at


**$6,950** (


[Nvidia marketplace](https://marketplace.nvidia.com/en-us/enterprise/personal-ai-supercomputers/dgx-spark/) ), and the retailers we checked start at


**$6,949.99** . Most computers get cheaper after launch. This one got pricier.


**Prices that move.** DeepSeek’s


**V4.1 Flash** is a million-token model under an MIT license, with about


**40 host listings** on


[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash/providers) (


[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) ). Early Thursday, by our own checks, the cheapest one changed twice in about an hour. Gas stations change prices slower than that.


**Now, the bad news.**


**PrimeIntellect** , one small host, raised its output price for gpt-oss-120b tenfold in a week, from


**$0.075** to


**$0.75** per million (


[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-oss-120b/providers) ). Same $10, a tenth of the tokens: about


**13 million instead of 133 million** . Free weights, surge pricing. So check more than one host.


**And some free weights don’t fit on any one desk.** Moonshot’s


**Kimi K3.1 Pro** has


**2.8 trillion parameters** (


[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro) ). Free to download. Bring a moving truck. At four bits a parameter, the weights alone take


**1.4 TB** . Apple’s biggest Mac Studio holds 512 GB, so you’d need


**three Macs** just to hold them. Kimi lives on rented hardware.


*Per-dollar verdict: for the model we checked, renting tokens wins on price. Owning wins on bragging rights.*


---


## The news: Nvidia signs for the AI build-out


Thursday we covered Nvidia’s sales. Today, what it signed for. The numbers are in the CFO commentary Nvidia filed with regulators this week (


[Nvidia CFO commentary, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000088/q3fy27cfocommentary.htm) ):


-


Nvidia has committed


**$390 billion** to its suppliers, up from


**$279 billion** a quarter earlier. Most of the increase is multi-year memory. Memory, bought years ahead. Nvidia meal-preps.


-


It also guarantees up to


**$118 billion** of what customers owe on data centers, more than its


**$115.8 billion** of sales last quarter. Most of it is SB Energy (


**$105 billion** ). The guarantees phase in building by building, the first expected in Nvidia’s fiscal 2029, which starts in early 2028.


Nvidia’s longest warranty this year covers somebody else’s rent.


*Per-dollar verdict: Nvidia now vouches for the rent. You’re still the one paying it.*


---


## B300s for resale


Ronit Jain of Liquid Compute, which describes itself as building a regulated exchange for compute, posted on X on Wednesday night. He says a staggering number of neoclouds (newer clouds built around AI chips) want his firm to resell B300 capacity first booked for Chinese-affiliated buyers, in the US and Western Europe instead, because of “concerns of stricter legislation” on serving China. We covered one of those rules on Thursday.


[Ronit Jain @ronitrjain I would expect B300 pricing to continue declining. A staggering number of neoclouds have approached us @liquidcompute looking to remarket long-term B300 capacity originally committed to Chinese-affiliated offtakers into the US and Western Europe due to concerns of stricter… 12:30 AM · Nov 19, 2026 · 368K Views 73 Replies · 119 Reposts · 853 Likes](https://x.com/ronitrjain/status/2123212182070370587)


Their compliance problem. Your shopping trip.


Jain expects B300 prices to keep falling. He didn’t say how far. Then again, his firm makes money on the trade.


*Per-dollar verdict: capacity booked for someone else could become your discount. If Jain’s right.*


---


## A bitcoin miner turned landlord


Earlier this month,


**Riot Platforms** signed a


**15-year lease** on its whole


**Corsicana, Texas** , campus. The tenant is an unnamed leading AI lab. Billions in rent, and no name on the mailbox.


-


The lease is worth


**$28 billion** , for


**910 megawatts** (


[Riot Q3 results](https://www.riotplatforms.com/riot-platforms-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-strategic-highlights/) ). Riot puts the rent at about


**$1.8 billion a year** , on average.


-


It covers power and land only. The tenant brings its own chips.


-


Counting all its leases, Riot now has about


**$38 billion** of long-term contracted revenue (


[Foley, which advised Riot](https://www.foley.com/news/2026/11/foley-advises-riot-platforms-on-28-billion-powered-land-lease-at-corsicana-campus/) ). This one deal is nearly


**three quarters** of that, by our math.


Fifteen years of rent. No halving.


*Per-dollar verdict: before you rent a chip, somebody’s renting the megawatts.*


All that to drive a future filled with


**Self-hosted Intelligence** .


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Chainsaw fueled. Spreadsheets open.


**Cut one: JSON key order.** AnyLanguageModel is a Swift library from Hugging Face. Its requests could come out with their keys in a different order each time. OpenAI’s prompt cache needs the same start on every request, so the cache never hit. A developer sorted the keys in a pull request on Thursday. In a 15-turn test with GPT-6.2 Sol, the cost of a run fell from


**$4.05** to about


**$0.50** , or


**88%** (


[pull request 432](https://github.com/huggingface/AnyLanguageModel/pull/432) ). All because a library couldn’t decide who goes first.


**The fine print:** it’s one benchmark, run through Azure, on a pull request that may not be merged yet. It only helps apps whose encoder shuffles keys.


**Cut two: caching.** Developer Carlos González ran


**366 million tokens** through Anthropic’s Claude Opus in one week. He pays for a $20 subscription; his tool estimates that week at


**$190.71** at API list prices.


**97%** of those tokens were cache reads, and he says that without caching it would have cost about


**$1,500** .


[Carlos M. González @cmglezpdev Opus is cheaper than you think. In one week, I used 366 million tokens with Opus 5.5 through Claude Code. I pay $20 a month for my subscription. T3 Code estimated that week's usage at $190.71 at API list prices. How do 366 million tokens on Opus come to just $190.71? An agent … 4:30 PM · Nov 18, 2026 · 238 Views 5 Replies · 6 Likes](https://x.com/cmglezpdev/status/2123091499848024367)


Somewhere, a pricing team just felt a chill. Caching is a Costco membership for déjà vu.


**The fine print:** those are his tool’s estimates, not an invoice. The $1,500 is his own what-if. And plan limits can change.


**Cut three: Mike P’s Mac Mini.** Mike P asked his Grok Bot why his usage runs low. Its answer: scripts on a Mac Mini do the grunt work, then hand the bot only the summary. Routines stay quiet unless something breaks, and each bot has one job.


[Mike P @mikepat711 Here is what my Grok Bot told me when I asked it about my setup and why my usage might be lower than others: Yes, a few things in your setup are pretty unusual, and most of them come down to keeping heavy work out of my sessions: - The Mac Mini does the grunt work. Scripts on… 2:35 AM · Nov 19, 2026 · 6.97K Views 14 Replies · 1 Repost · 58 Likes](https://x.com/mikepat711/status/2123243670249840652)


The bot hired an intern. The intern is a Mac Mini.


**The fine print:** that’s the bot talking, no bill attached. And work handed to a second assistant gets billed on that plan instead.


The best token is the one you already paid for.
